items.text: Hello everyone! We're pushing a small hotfix today to resolve some outstanding issues with By God Alone and the Crozier Update. This hotfix should be fully compatible with existing 1.20x saves and mods.
Please check the changelog below for more information!
Fixed a bug for resizing text in College of Cardinals that could appear in languages other than English
Fixed a bug where the revoke interaction could break the UI in languages other than English
Fixed a bug where Russian rites and faith names would use cut-off adjectives
Fixed a number of crashes that could occur when rendering portraits
Fixed a bug where monasteries could not be bestowed to monastic holy orders
Fixed a bug where the create holy site button was hidden without By God Alone despite meeting non-DLC related requirements
Fixed a bug where dying as an adventurer after procuring an estate left you landless and would trigger a game over
Religious Artifact inspirations no longer show up without By God Alone, as they could not be sponsored without it

Hello everybody! We're releasing Update 1.20.1 today to tackle issues and balance concerns reported by players since the release of By God Alone and the 1.20 "Crozier" Update. We'll continue addressing your feedback and bug reports, but given the relatively short time until the release of Silk & Silver, we will be targeting its accompanying 1.21 Update release for any changes going forward.
Check the changelog below for more information!
Added historical sainthood and burial sites for Clotilde, Sigismund, Guntram, Sigebert III, and William of Gellone.
The Monk trait is now selectable in the Ruler Designer.
Custom rulers can now be created for landless Archbishops and Cardinals.
Updated the Confucian saint designation from Shengxian to Xianru.
Added historical glossary to some tenets, separating their historical background links from their descriptions and names.
Added auto-fill buttons when editing Rite names.
Ask Subordinates for Gold now costs between 100 and 250 Piety, scaling with the amount of Gold requested.
Spiritual Fulfillment from Cranial Trophies now scales with the victim’s Prestige.
Religious Scholar's lifestyle XP bonus is halved, from up to +50% to up to +25%.
Passive rite learning while travelling has a 90-day cooldown instead of 30.
Beseech De Jure Rights has a 3-year cooldown for the asker instead of a per-cleric one.
Characters who gain raiding through a personal tenet can no longer use the default Pillage intent.
Request White Peace now requires the war to have lasted at least two years.
Ecumenical Council debates now have an AI opponent who makes their own sway attempts and cannot be swayed, unless a player already leads the opposing side.
Negotiate for Land can now request a primary title, with harder acceptance and only the small refusal penalty for its holder.
Heads of Faith on the mainline rite can still use Sway to My Rite to call Heads of Rite back to it, at a substantial acceptance penalty.
Befriending a Head of Faith at a feast now retains the Befriend scheme until friendship is established and shows potential friendship in their event.
Added a recipient cooldown to Bestow De Jure Lands.
Heads of Faith now take two Feasts to befriend, and clergy claim and land negotiations are harder to chain.
Removed the high minimum chance for AI rulers to accept petitions.
Reduced Study Rite success bonuses: Learning now contributes ×2 instead of ×3, each Piety level contributes +3 instead of +5, and Theologian contributes +10 instead of +20.

Ecumenical Council sways now scale with the size of the proposed change, up to 2.5 times the base cost. Free trait-based sways affect fewer attendees for major changes, and duels over radical proposals are slightly harder.
Independent kings and emperors of at least Paragon of Virtue Piety can now create Holy Sites in their realm when the county follows their faith and their Head of Faith has a positive opinion of them.
Rebalanced Assume the Conqueror’s Mantle around the Become Conqueror requirements and set its Piety cost to 3,000.
Raised Canonize a Saint’s base costs from 2,000 to 3,000 Piety and from 300 to 500 Gold, and added an opinion requirement when Head of Faith approval is needed.
Editing the mainline rite now requires proposed tenets to be at least Very Popular.
Grand Cathedral bell contributions no longer require a city or temple holding in the contributor’s domain.
The AI no longer declares war on the Frankokratia leader while the Fourth Crusade story is running.
The AI now respects its relations with a banner’s dynasty when deciding whether to gift it.
The AI now only revokes titles for a rival or wrong-faith vassal when doing so would not incur Tyranny.
Nomad invasion AI avoids island kingdom targets again.
The AI now respects Influence and Honor limits when harming title candidacies.
AI vassals can now use Claim Throne when enabled by a Struggle, even if they are not powerful vassals.
AI diarchs now recruit heads of powerful families for coups, allowing coups to work in realms without powerful vassals.
A new AI Pope no longer recasts a core tenet of a rite a player edited.
AI attendees can no longer sway back Ecumenical Council attendees who have already been swayed during the current debate.
The AI now avoids demanding children for the cloister who are married, have children, or are heirs, and remembers refusals.
AI clerics no longer adopt other rulers’ heirs or player courtiers as theocratic heirs.
The AI Pope no longer appoints a player’s unlanded courtiers as Cardinals.
The AI no longer demands vows of chastity from chaste characters.
AI Ecumenical Council hosts now generally propose the nearest doctrine change, with exceptions for Heralds, Heresiarchs, madness, or strong preferences.
Emperors can restore Backwater counties, and the AI now takes the decision.
The AI no longer overrides its restriction against choosing Eastern-rite Cardinals before the Great Schism.
Before the Great Schism the Patriarch of Constantinople cannot become a cardinal, and the AI only picks Western-rite cardinals.
AI clergy invitations to Ecumenical Councils now follow clerical gender doctrine rather than ruling gender, allowing councils to reach quorum.
Chaplain auto-fill prefers the owner's rite, and AI heads of faith only seat archbishops of their own rite.
AI rulers of Meritocratic Khanates no longer indiscriminately raze holdings.
New AI Popes, including Populist candidates, only make vice or abomination tenets core when an Ecumenical Council would allow it.
The AI no longer spends a player lessee’s Treasury on building construction.
Fixed wide character animations being cut off in large event windows.
Beseech De Jure Rights now explains its Iberian Struggle restriction.
Fixed bookmarks map highlight not appearing when quickly moving the mouse between characters.
Proclaim the Kingdom of Heaven now shows how many qualifying counties you hold and how many you need.
Bodyguard court position requirements now display correctly for non-nomadic rulers.
Funeral activity UI now shows scaled costs.
Council task notifications now correctly display their descriptions when referring to councillor skill.
Added a letter from the Head of Faith when you become a Cardinal through College seeding or a successful request.
Fixed the Factions window being empty after taking your liege's title while the "Against your Liege" tab was selected.
Every successful Ecumenical Council tenet debate now explains the Conservatives’ resentment toward the host and Innovators.
Failing to murder an attendee or to have an attendee expelled during an Ecumenical Council now shows a negative notification instead of a positive one.
The duels to expel a badly dressed attendee and to negotiate an alliance during an Ecumenical Council now describe their success and failure outcomes.
Leveraging your position to reassure your Court Chaplain before an Ecumenical Council now shows both possible outcomes and notifies you when the attempt fails.
Other players attending an Ecumenical Council now receive notifications naming attendees swayed to the Innovators or Conservatives.
Coats of Arms in the Clerical Regions map mode now display information about the clerical title rather than the holder’s realm.
Fixed cardinals missing from the Landless Rulers list in the game start lobby.
The plus icon on an unused artifact slot in your holy site is now always visible.
Fixed “Joining” text overflowing the multiplayer lobby.
Fixed a bug where Character interactions would show as unavailable after opening an Artifact interaction.
The Resume Court Event alert now works when the event is in your own Royal Court.
Fixed the Royal Court disappearing again after it finished loading.
Choose Career Path, Found Kingdom, Found Empire, and Consecrate Kingdom now correctly open on their descriptions.
The Legend creation alert now uses the discounted creation cost.
Fixed a missing string in the Find Adherent Scheme progress breakdown.
Influence Clerical Candidacy is now unavailable when the candidate already holds every eligible title.
Fixed the Spiritual Fulfillment sorting in the Personal Beliefs window being inverted.
Improved Tenet, Doctrine, and Personal Tenet tooltips.
Fixed long localized contract names pushing tier labels and close buttons out of place.
Fixed the number of remaining holy relics being cut off in other languages.
Clergy list rows no longer appear clickable when they are not.
Added an empty-list message to Christian Church history when no history has been recorded.
Adjusted spacing in the Rite section of events.
Updated page-turning buttons in the Christian Church chapter book to better match its artwork.
Map mode close buttons now remain visible.
Fixed text in popup notifications overlapping with buttons.
Editing a Rite's name, adjective or icon now properly applies the desired changes.
You can now select Clerical Region holders through the Clerical Regions mapmode in lobby.
Tournament phase descriptions now display correctly in planning tooltips.
The Faith map mode now displays landless and landed religious heads, with a toggle between religious heads and Holy Sites.
Fixed the deceased character’s portrait overlapping other portraits in the Funeral activity window.
The Title window now clearly marks same-tier titles that will follow the primary title under Appointment succession.
The Customize Route window now hides when other right-side windows open, preventing overlap.
Title interactions now correctly highlight the selected region on the map.
Fixed the Health tooltip breaking for ill characters over 50.
Interaction window will now properly display the puppet as sender when you send an interaction through one.
The Great Project UI will now prioritize puppets that can actually start the projects.
When starting a scheme through a puppet, the puppet will be shown in the start scheme window instead of the puppeteer.
Fixed a visual glitch with the active color picker in the Barbershop.
Grand Cathedral planning tooltips now clearly identify the future owner.
The Raise Army tooltip now explains splitting armies according to supply limits, and Ctrl-click is clearly labeled “Raise without splitting”.
The outermost Spiritual Fulfillment levels can now be hovered in both tooltips and the Personal Beliefs window.
Ecumenical Council logs now record attendees’ starting factions and player choices in each debate, and vote results show the numbers supporting Innovators and Conservatives.
Fixed long character tab names and player-heir text overflowing the Character window.
Fixed long text stretching the Domicile, Archdiocese, and Legend windows.
Fixed long text overflowing the Holy Site, Puppet, potential puppet, and Rite creation windows.
Fixed long localized text extending beyond the Title window.
Improved spacing, margins, and alignment in the Christian Church and other By God Alone windows.
The main menu now waits for its character portraits to be ready, without getting stuck waiting for portraits that cannot load.
Adjusted the Gold and Treasury transfer button to align correctly with UI skins.
Adjusted the size and position of Puppet Action banners in the Holy Site window.
Clerical Region Coats of Arms now appear at the clerical title’s preferred capital rather than the holder’s actual capital.
Fixed missing labels for Situation map modes.
Learned Tenet notifications now display their header icon correctly.
Added a Schism progress view to the Christian Church window, with progress, stance information, crisis indicators, and relevant decisions.
Fixed Christian Church tabs resetting and portrait icons flashing when the window first opens.
Added Shift+F2 as a shortcut to the Royal Court.
Adding a Personal Tenet now asks for confirmation.
Improved candidacy buttons and fallback interactions for different succession systems, including cases where no valid clerical title is available.
Fixed long governor names and Merit values pushing candidacy information or interaction buttons outside their windows.
Fixed long College of Cardinals descriptions and names overflowing their space.
Improved treasury withdrawal tooltip placement so its locked tooltip remains usable, and restored the request funds button where councillor checks incorrectly hid it.
Removed duplicate names from puppet interaction lists and improved the Puppet view.
Character interaction lists now reset their custom sorting correctly when refreshed.
Secret descriptions now identify the forbidden Personal Tenet involved.
Hidden tenets that cannot be picked from activity tenet selection lists.
Added missing empty-list text and hid the unused footer when no Holy Order decisions are available.
Light heresy divergence now notifies affected players rather than the entire faith, and heresy spread messages also reach the convert’s liege.
Decisions with option lists, including Recruit from Nomadic Capital, Adopt a Centralized Bureaucracy, and Petition the Liege, now open on the list instead of preselecting an option.
Rite-change notifications now correctly list permitted and forbidden tenets and show their Spiritual Fulfillment effects.
Added icons for the Gift Claim and Incite Claim War interactions.
Added flat versions of character interaction icons for use within windows.
Female cardinals now wear the red cardinal hat instead of the clergy crown.
Improved the Civil secret category icon to reduce jagged edges.
Added a standalone Lifestyle trait background texture.
Painting relics no longer appear as floating boxes in wall artifact slots.
Increased the texture resolution of small Tenet banner backgrounds.
Added new flat icon for Rites.
Added an alert icon for losing land through clerical succession.
Portrait pattern masks now retain a minimum resolution at each graphics quality setting.
Non-Chinese Han empresses no longer use the Chinese imperial bedroom background.
Improved the resolution of the Holy Site header banner and reduced pixelation of plague level icons.
Updated the Cardinal marker above Coats of Arms and the Coronation Regalia building icon.
Corrected the Crusade chapter illustration and improved chapter illustration cropping.
Fixed portraits flickering when zooming or rotating.
Corrected the Frankish haircut’s Ruler Designer checks.
Eastern faiths now use appropriate backgrounds for conversion and Court Chaplain displays.
The wandering priest event now uses a more appropriate outfit.
Spouses of the Huangdi now correctly receive clothing.
Fixed domicile buildings not playing their sounds, and gave ecclesiastical buildings more appropriate sound effects.
Non-ecumenical Christian faiths no longer receive 0% Church Obligations.
Non-Christian Heads of Faith who receive land now immediately gain clergy courtiers, ensuring that Clerical Appointment has an eligible heir.
Starting the Crusade chapter now resets both the Crusade decision cooldown and the Crusade papal bull cooldown.
Players without By God Alone are no longer papal candidates, since becoming Pope would end their game.
Corrected the Greek name of Cratea to Krateia and removed the duplicate Tanais name from Kuzeytorg.
The Archdiocese of York is part of England in 1178 instead of independent.
The Carolingian, Nestorian and Adoptionist rites now get an appropriate core tenet on game start.
Dead cardinals keep the Cardinal title instead of being called Duke-Bishop.
Replacing Jaromir in the relevant bookmark event now makes Jan a theological agent puppet when eligible.
A Resplendent Acclamation now awards or costs Piety rather than Influence for governments that do not use Influence.
Cardinal kindred voting reasons now compare the same papabile priority scores shown in the College of Cardinals.
Secular devoted rulers can no longer be granted an ecclesiastical title that would flip their realm to theocracy.
Mend the Great Schism is available in the Crusades and Conversion chapters.
Study Faith and Learn Language schemes cancel when the target is imprisoned.
Study Scripture event options now correctly reward rulers who do not use Treasury.
What's in a Bed? no longer offers a broken expert option when the court expert is employed but unavailable.
Childhood personality events now pair Cynical with Zealous and Trusting with Paranoid.
867 Iberian prelates use regional cultures again.
Rogier Hermanszoon no longer retains outdated county claims in 1066.
Corrected 1178 character-history anachronisms for Werner of Winterthur and an easter egg character.
Stained glass cathedral contributions use the same contributor checks as sibling contributions.
Counts can now correctly see and start Playdate activities.
Fixed a nomadic hunt event being unable to fire for the activity host.
Demand Church Succession now correctly recognizes targets inside a cardinal-archbishop's clerical region.
The historical Adoptionism conversion event now unlocks the faith before attempting conversion.
AI requests for anointment now prompt a player-controlled religious authority instead of being granted automatically.
Request Excommunication now checks piety on every path instead of only the puppet path.
Mending the Great Schism now recognizes a puppeted Orthodox or Catholic Head of Faith as supportive.
Assume the Conqueror’s Mantle is now hidden for landless adventurers and only awards its rewards when you accept the Conqueror’s path.
Make Puppet through Negotiate Release now uses the same character, Piety, Dread, and Hook requirements as Make External Ruler Puppet.
Characters whose faith has Sacred Destruction now raid to destroy rather than pillage, matching characters with the personal tenet.
Koblenz is now held by Theutgaud of Trier in 867, with Bertolf succeeding him in 869 as in Trier.
No Sicilian characters exist before the culture is created in 950.
Puppets advice now waits until adulthood.
The pilgrim badge theft event can only happen once every 5 years, like the other badge events.
The Accepted same-sex relations game rule applies to every rite, not only each faith's main rite.
Grand Cathedral start and completion events now reach each contributor once, regardless of the number of contributions.
An Eastern-rite Pope now becomes Catholic when the Great Schism occurs.
Grand Cathedrals can no longer replace existing Great Buildings, including the Capital Temple Complex.
Seek Communion is now available with the Chalcedonian Pope before the Great Schism.
Clergy can no longer legitimize lowborn bastards.
Aquitaine's duchies are de jure French again from 877, so the Kingdom of Aquitaine no longer reappears in 1066.
Beseech De Jure Rights can no longer move a kingdom beneath your empire while you are involved in the Iberian Struggle.
Inspection funding now costs Piety rather than Gold when required by the relevant tenet.
Popes who take the name of an early Pope, such as Linus or Petrus, now get a regnal number.
The Investiture Council summons phase lasts 3 months in multiplayer too, so distant prelates can arrive.
Restoring Carantania now places the kingdom in the de jure empire its duchies came from.
Marshal knight training events can pick knights who are not busy with an activity again.
Winning a challenger war against the Shia Caliph now promotes your existing title to Head of Faith rather than granting a duplicate title.
Fixed a crash when displaying scheme agent slots in the Intrigue window.
Abandoning a holy site always returns its enshrined relics to the county holder.
The Archdiocese of Salzburg goes to Karlmann's Bavaria instead of staying with East Francia when Ludwig the German dies.
Corrected the 867 Archbishop history for York and Trier, including duplicate Ecgbert characters, gaps in succession, and Theutgaud’s excommunication.
The Cyril and Methodius story continues when Rostislav dies before the brothers leave for Rome.
New Cardinals are divorced when their rite forbids clerical marriage.
Baptistery bonuses now apply to their owner’s conversion attempts as well as their vassals’.
Carolingian-rite rulers can restore the Holy Roman Empire.
Updated the Gnostic special doctrine to match the reworked Gnosticism tenet and removed duplicate tenets from three Dualist rites.
Randomly generated temple holders now respect the granting ruler’s gender rules.
Holy Sites added to Chalcedonianism before the Great Schism now pass to the Church that holds their clerical region.
Adopt State Rite converts rulers of another faith instead of silently doing nothing.
Plague outbreaks cost a character Spiritual Fulfillment at most once every three years.
Send Legatine Mission is now only available for participants in the Christian Church situation.
An Unreliable Steed now adds Stress for traits that dislike an option instead of relieving it.
Request Elevation is now unavailable while the petitioner is Incapable or imprisoned.
Created and split archbishoprics now follow the primary heir, ensuring they survive their first Archbishop.
The Council of Toledo outcome modifier now only applies to Mozarabic rulers.
Evangelize the Pagans now actually converts the target to the evangelizer’s faith and rite when successful.
Negotiate Release counts Make Puppet and Change Prison as demands.
Roger de Pont L’Eveque now appears only once in 1178, holding both North Riding and the Archdiocese of York.
Landless adventurers no longer pay prestige upkeep for a Bodyguard.
Victorious Antipopes now move to Rome with their capital, allowing petitions to work correctly.
Non-Christian spiritual Heads of Faith now retain Clerical Appointment succession and an eligible heir.
Converting a character to another character’s or county’s faith now also copies the corresponding rite.
The College of Cardinals now retains eligible candidates when the Pope’s main rite adopts Lay Clergy.
Failing to murder your Nemesis during an Ecumenical Council no longer turns them back into a Rival.
Fixed script errors when selecting the doctrine for an Ecumenical Council’s third debate.
Saint Imre is now buried in Veszprém rather than sharing Székesfehérvár with Saint István.
The Pope and Ecumenical Patriarch can no longer change faith before the Great Schism.
Chalcedonianism now unlocks Great Holy Wars under the same historical conditions as Catholicism.
Players can now comply with or defy a Church-imposed white peace, and the AI only requests one when needed.
Restored the “of Place” designation for unlanded nobles, including heirs and consorts.
Request Anointment and the Pope’s Cardinal orders are no longer blocked by diplomatic range.
A puppet Pope no longer excommunicates his own puppeteer.
Holy Orders will now stick with their Rite when it diverges to a new Faith.
The Invite to Coup interaction is now visible when appropriate.
Fixed a rare crash that could occur if a council task would invalidate itself or destroy the council when completing.
Fixed a crash that could rarely occur when updating Dynasty modifiers.
The Christian Church situation no longer ends incorrectly when Rome is controlled by an Orthodox ruler.
Invite to Court no longer poaches other courts' knights, councillors, court-position holders and wards.
Expand the Steppe for Siberia removes Siberian Permafrost again.
Fixed the relatedness calculation for A Perfect Circle so the achievement unlocks for the family tree described.
Adventurers hired as mercenaries by a defending war leader now get paid when the war ends.
Personal tenet holders now gain or lose Spiritual Fulfillment when their rite permits or prohibits that tenet.
The Father, the Son, and the Holy Grandson achievement now advances correctly on player succession.
Organization Coats of Arms now match their Head of Faith or Head of Rite titles where possible.
Cardinals who become landless adventurers now give up their cardinalate first, so their land passes to the inheritor instead of staying with the adventurer.
Archbishops and cardinals keep their ecclesiastical government and archdiocese when their rite adopts Lay Clergy, instead of being turned feudal.
A holding with a pending grant to a monastic order can no longer be granted to a second order, and an answered grant no longer re-leases an already leased holding.
Saints canonized before the Great Schism are now saints of both Catholicism and Orthodoxy, including at post-1054 starts.
Stage an Act of Devotion is no longer available to landless adventurers.
Ludwig the German’s designated heir is now cleared if the historical partition conditions no longer apply at his death.
Ludwig the Younger is the designated heir of Ludwig the German in 867, so East Francia keeps Mainz and Hamburg and Karlmann still gets Bavaria.
Odo of Bayeux starts 1066 as the ecclesiastical ruler of Bayeux, and of Kent while he holds it.
Removed 53 unused Holy Site definitions that prevented their baronies, including Meroe, from becoming Holy Sites, and fixed the Adopt Holy Site tooltip displaying a raw key.
Losing or replacing a personal tenet now removes its Spiritual Fulfillment, preventing repeated tenet swaps from generating extra Fulfillment.
Theocratic children can be chosen as favourite child.
The Heroic Bloodline legend creation discount now lowers the creation cost.
Characters of every rite of the Pope's faith can request cardinalates and take part in the College before the Great Schism.
Hugo the Abbot starts 867 as an ecclesiastical ruler and a monk.
Deaths from Fragile Bones, drinking, and chronic illness now count as natural deaths for Mandala devotion succession.
Stillbirth events roll the child's gender once, so the description and the tooltip match.
Request Claim on Ireland looks for Irish counties outside the Roman rite instead of outside Catholicism.
Western missionaries and merchants in nomad events are Chalcedonian until the Great Schism, so Catholicism no longer appears early.
Great Holy War requirements now display their cooldown outside debug mode.
Write Muwashshah Poem lets you choose what to do with the poem instead of always selling it.
The Cathedral School only boosts children at courts in its own archdiocese instead of across the realm.
Appoint as Republican Overseer can no longer turn clergy or theocratic vassals into republics.
Demand Conversion is now unavailable for clerical region holders whose capital does not already follow your faith, preventing them from becoming adventurers.
Requesting excommunication of a duke or lower through a local cleric checks the target instead of the cleric.
Nizar’s anti-caliphate no longer requires By God Alone.
Daoxue becomes available from 1050 in games started in 867, so it can be converted to, reformed and branched.
Incite Claim War no longer offers the target or yourself as the attacker, so a ruler cannot be incited against themselves.
Landed children who run away to become adventurers now relinquish their titles to their heir, with all options explaining the effect.
Non-Christian clerical courts now receive clergy courtiers at game start and every three years, ensuring Clerical Appointment has candidates.
Become an Adventurer now explains why Heads of Faith cannot take the decision.
Hasan Sabbah's story follows the Nizari rite instead of the whole Shia faith.
The Minister of Rites no longer receives inappropriate clergy interactions, including Request New Court Chaplain at ministry courts and external clerical puppeting.
Losing an Apprehend Adventurer war imprisons the adventurer and seizes their possessions but no longer disbands their camp.
A rival losing land now only changes your Stress, rather than also changing your Spiritual Fulfillment.
The letter announcing a new Antipope goes to players of the Antipope's religion instead of always to Christians.
Theocrats can no longer take Convert to Confucianism or Convert to Taoism, which took their theocratic title into the new faith.
New nobles generated when granting titles now follow your rite as well as your culture.
Zealous Missionary Ascension now converts counties to the adventurer’s rite.
The Far From Home traveler and their family now convert to your rite.
Refusing a large Negotiate for Land request now applies the Church Authority penalty once rather than three times.
Fixed a softlock when a landless Noble Family title holder becomes independent.
The Gender Equality game rule now correctly applies to all rites rather than only the mainline rite.
Ecumenical Council debate events can now fire correctly in multiplayer.
For Life clerical appointment now retains the realm priest selected by the player or Church instead of replacing them with a theocratic vassal.
Guido's Guiding Light stays achievable after Guido dies, for a game started as Guido.
Characters serving in an army can no longer host Feasts.
Landless adventurers can no longer host an Ecumenical Council they are barred from attending.
Fervent Proselytism’s easier Ascension requirements now correctly apply to players.
Influence Cardinal Vote lets a papabile cardinal ask for votes for themselves.
Chalcedonianism can no longer establish a Head of Faith before the Great Schism even without By God Alone.
Light heresy divergence no longer rewrites rites led by a player Head of Rite.
Court chaplains of another rite in the same faith stay valid after a rite conversion, and the candidate pool is no longer empty.
Find a New Faith for Persia's conversion priest follows the chosen rite instead of the faith's main rite.
Sway Vassal and Sway Ruler to My Rite can no longer target the Head of a Rite, so an archbishop can no longer convert the Pope to his rite.
Reformation no longer removes dynamic holy sites from the reformed faith.
Chinese Ministers now have a line of succession again and can retire in peace.
Puppet interaction cooldowns now apply to the puppet rather than the puppeteer.
Reforming a rite no longer changes the old rite’s name.
Fixed getting stuck on a white screen when you cancel creating a new ironman game.
A new diarch is now appointed correctly when an invalid diarch is removed.
Heresies now keep spreading before their declaration and convert rulers along with their counties.
Reforming a faith now correctly converts its adherents, including court and realm, preventing Game Over conditions on succession.
Grand Cathedrals in a clerical region can now only be built in its capital, with tooltips explaining the restriction.
The Isolated Capital modifier is now removed when a county changes hands, except through succession.
Without Khans of the Steppe, rulers made Tribal at game start now lose the Unruly Nomads law and receive Tribal Authority.
Claim Title now correctly lists eligible county-tier and higher titles.
Negotiate Release now only offers Make Puppet when the prisoner can become your puppet, and no longer allows clergy to become ruler puppets.
Faiths with Lay Clergy can now found Military Orders without requiring a theocracy or clerical puppet.
Grand Cathedral Master Mason contributions now accept the ruler’s own Stewardship as stated in the tooltip, and the AI-only founder exemption can no longer apply to players.
Landless clerical region holders now relinquish their clerical titles when becoming adventurers.
Partially completed disaster relief projects no longer trigger a Dynastic Cycle catalyst.
Puppeteers and realm priests can now contribute to Grand Cathedrals.
A newly appointed Pope who is not Head of Faith no longer incorrectly updates the main rite after the Great Schism.
History-only rites, including Nabi, Tabi’un, and Sahabah, can no longer be selected for custom rulers, converted to, or targeted by Find Adherent schemes.
Corrected historical rites for several starting counties, including Byzantine rites in southern Italy and Paphlagonia, and Maliki rites in Palermo and Tunis that persist through the Great Schism.
The Create Holy Site button is no longer available without By God Alone.
Clerical title requests are now hidden when the faith has a temporal Head of Faith.
Offering a Hook in relevant interactions now requires that the Hook can actually be added.
Clerical Region split and merge interactions now correctly check faith, including cases involving a Minister of Rites of a different faith.
Clergy organization membership now updates correctly for courtiers and when the Clergy trait is lost.
Vassal Heads of Faith can now use the Cardinal Treasury budget law.
Landless adventurers can now influence their own clerical candidacy and buy a clerical title for themselves.
Theocratic and ecclesiastical rulers can now grant Feudal, Clan, and Tribal governments where permitted.
Clan-inclined nomadic rulers can now grant Clan government to eligible recipients.
Dynastic marriage now correctly blocks close-family matches.
Corrected gender penalties in Appointment candidate scoring.
Fixed the administrative authority surcharge in Feudalize Holding costs.
The Coterie dynasty legacy now checks the correct character scope.
Holy War restrictions in the Iberian Struggle’s Conciliation phase now correctly check culture.
Tribal Authority requirements for reforming pagan faiths now only apply to Tribal rulers.
Custom rulers following disabled rites can now branch a new rite.
Restore Temporal Rule is now hidden for Heads of Faith and Heads of Rite.
Petition the Pope is now hidden when its requirements do not apply.
Ask for Gold and Seek Indulgences no longer appear on an inappropriate Court Chaplain when an Archbishop is available.
The Pope can no longer use Split Clerical Region or Ask Subordinates for Gold on an Antipope.
Great Schism progress now correctly counts wars between kings.
Church participant groups now recalculate after the Great Schism.
Domicile religious data now follows the rite rather than only the parent faith, with compatibility handling for existing data.
Stopping the would-be Anchorite now gives that character the Reclusive trait rather than giving it to the player.
Court claim events no longer fire for claims that cannot be used.
House renaming now uses synchronized base names, avoiding empty or unsynchronized house names.
Landless counties are no longer counted as ordinary counties in interface data functions.
Corrected the culture reference used by the Visigothic Codes tradition.
Faith and rite creation now correctly enforce doctrine incompatibilities for Natural Primitivism and Polyamory.
Fixed crashes when modifier effects or triggers reference missing static modifiers, or when a map icon widget cannot be created.
Fixed a potential multiplayer out-of-sync caused by localized cultural names.

Hello everyone! By God Alone, our latest Core Expansion for Crusader Kings III, is now available alongside the free 1.20.0 "Crozier" Update.

In By God Alone, being a good ruler and being a good believer aren't always the same thing. Your characters will wrestle with sin as they try to live up to their faith's ideals, while navigating the rich and evolving political landscape of the Christian Church. Stir up religious debates (or bring them to an end), decide where the authority of the crown ends and the cross begins, and weigh your ambitions against the fate of your soul.
By God Alone is available as part of Crusader Kings III: Chapter V, or as an individual purchase. Check out our release trailer below, followed by the changelog.

Added the Christian Church, a Situation covering all of Christendom. Every Christian ruler of County tier or above is a participant. All participants share the same Chapter, modifiers, and Great Schism progress.
Participants are sorted into six groups. The Main Power is the Christian Faith that holds the most Counties.
Main Power (Clerical)
Main Power (Secular)
Secondary Powers (Clerical)
Secondary Powers (Secular)
Heretics (Clerical)
Heretics (Secular)
The Situation moves through Chapters. Each Chapter has its own Religion, Subject, Diplomacy, and Warfare modifiers, applied differently to each participant group.
Chapters come in four types: Stability, Zeal, Instability, and Crisis. A Crisis Chapter can end in the Great Schism once Schism progress has reached its threshold.

Added the Guide the Christian Church decision, available once every ten years. It triggers a Catalyst of your choice and pushes the Situation toward the Chapter you want. Taken as Head of Faith, it has four times the effect.
Added the Christian Church window. It shows the current Chapter, participant groups, active modifiers, and Great Schism progress, with sub-windows for All Phases and History.
Added events for the Saeculum Obscurum, Conversion, and Reform Chapters.

notes.title: Clerical Titles, Clerical Regions, and the Ecclesiastical Government​

items.text: Added the Ecclesiastical Government for Christian clergy. Ecclesiastical rulers hold land as an office of the Church, and their titles pass by clerical succession.

Added Clerical Titles and Clerical Regions, the Church's own spheres of influence parallel to the secular one. An Archdiocese is a Clerical Region held by an Archbishop. Its seat is the Clerical Region Capital, the County the region was founded on.
Added ecclesiastical titles with holder history for 867, 1066, and 1178, including Aksum, Antioch, Alexandria, and Jerusalem.
Clerical Regions can be founded on any held title of Duchy tier or above.
Clerical Regions convert neighboring Counties to their holder's Rite over time
Added a Clerical Regions map mode. It shows each see's holder and Rite, and stripes Counties whose Rite differs from the region's.
Added Lease Contracts. They set the terms between a secular ruler, the clergy leasing land inside their realm, and the clergy's Religious Superior.
Church Obligations are set at Minimal, Mild, or Strong Centralization. They decide how much the leasing clergy contributes upward to their Religious Superior.
Secular Obligations are set as Personal or Fixed. They decide how much the leasing clergy contributes to the secular ruler's income.
Religious Superiors and Religious Subordinates form a hierarchy parallel to the feudal one, for both Theocratic and Ecclesiastical clergy.
All clergy of a Faith now belong to that Faith's clerical organization. The link is used for succession and other functions.
The Ecclesiastical Government uses a church Treasury. Most regular Treasury income comes from local income, unlike Administrative Treasuries, which are filled from a central point.
Ecclesiastical and Theocratic rulers can hold any Temple holding directly. Temples in their domain that they do not hold directly are held by a Baron-tier Ecclesiastical vassal.
When Ecclesiastical Rulers hold multiple titles of their primary Tier, the non-primary titles are kept together with the primary one on succession.
Added Ecclesiastical Laws covering Cardinal benefices. A benefice grants a Cardinal a special Treasury income paid by the Pope.
Added Clerical Elective and Clerical Appointment succession for Church seats. Clerical appointments favor the holder's own clergy and greater sees, and penalize candidates from outside the clergy.

notes.title: Added decisions for rulers with clergy in their realm

items.text: Levy the Tithes: demand gold from every Theocratic and Ecclesiastical vassal in your realm.
Educate your Clerical Court: ordain, instruct, or recruit clergy for your court.
Seize the Clerical Region: take the Clerical Region your capital lies in. If the seat is held, its Archbishop is deposed.

notes.title: Added interactions for managing Clerical Titles

items.text: Create Clerical Title: found a Clerical Title inside a ruler's realm, seated on the de jure capital of the title you pick.
Expand Clerical Title: grow a Clerical Region into an adjacent de jure Duchy held by rulers of your Faith.
Merge Clerical Title: absorb a neighboring Clerical Title and all of its Counties.
Split Clerical Title: carve the part of a Clerical Region that lies inside a chosen ruler's realm into a new Clerical Title, and grant it to a cleric of your choice.

Replace Archbishop: depose an Archbishop and give their Clerical Title to a worthier cleric. Deposing an Archbishop of another Rite costs far more Piety, needs higher Learning than theirs, and weakens your Faith's Fervor.
Grant Clerical Title: give an existing Clerical Title to a cleric. If the seat is held, the current holder is deposed.
Buy Clerical Title: purchase a Clerical Title from its holder. Available to Faiths with the Simony tenet.

Request Elevation: petition the Head of Faith for the Clerical Title of your own Clerical Region, whether it is vacant or held by your superior. It grants the whole clerical domain, cannot unseat players, and has a low acceptance chance.
Request New Court Chaplain: ask for a replacement Court Chaplain, drawn from courtiers in your realm.
Request Church Treasury: ask your Religious Superior or Subordinate for gold from their treasury.
Demand Church Succession: make yourself the fallback heir to a cleric's lands should they die without a rightful heir. Piety cost scales with the tier of the realm pledged.
Request Enforced Succession: ask a cleric to compel the holder of a title you have a claim on to yield it to their rightful heir.
Preach My Legitimacy: spend Piety to have a cleric's priests raise your Legitimacy.
Added Influence Clerical Candidacy: spend Piety to raise or lower a candidate's score for a Clerical Title.

notes.title: Added interactions for land and claims

items.text: Beseech Claim: gain a claim on one of a ruler's titles with the help of an Ecclesiastical ruler or your Head of Faith.
Negotiate For Land: take vassals or titles you have a claim or de jure right to, with the help of an Ecclesiastical ruler.
Bestow Title: as a cleric, grant a title that does not yet exist directly to someone, possibly raising their rank.
Bestow De Jure Lands: as a cleric, add a neighboring title to a ruler's de jure territory.
Beseech De Jure Rights: ask a cleric to make a neighboring title a de jure part of your primary title.
Consecrate Kingdom: as a cleric, create a new Kingdom for someone and gain a Hook on them in return.
Incite Holy War: urge a ruler to declare a holy war.
Incite Claim War: urge a ruler to press a claim by war.
Request Victory: ask a cleric to declare your war against another Christian ruler won, once you hold at least 90% War Score.
Request White Peace: ask a cleric to mediate a white peace with another Christian ruler.
Offer Spiritual Counsel: offer private counsel in exchange for a Hook.
Seek Communion: petition the Head of Faith to receive your Faith back into the Church, ending its status as a heresy.
Demand Divorce: demand that someone put aside a spouse whose marriage offends the Faith, or can be made to look that way.

Demand Chastity: demand a vow of chastity. While the vow holds, the target takes a lasting Fertility penalty and cannot start a seduction or courtship. Lustful characters find a forced vow harder to bear. The vow can be shed with the Renounce Vow of Chastity decision.
Theocratic and Ecclesiastical rulers are now playable. Theocratic rulers get their own government type and succession.
Added Designate Theocratic Heir: name your preferred heir to your theocratic title.
Added the Adopt Theocratic Rule decision, which converts your government to a Theocracy, and the Restore Temporal Rule decision, which converts a Theocracy back to Feudal.
Theocratic gender succession follows the Clerical Gender doctrine.
Theocratic titles can interact with factions.
Theocracies can only declare religious wars.
Clerical rulers can divorce on their own authority. Where dynastic approval applies, they ask their house head.
Clergy of a marrying Faith can take the Renounce Vows decision, which removes the Devoted trait so they can marry again.
The Court Chaplain of a Clergy Ruler is always going to endorse them.
Added the College of Cardinals and Cardinal Titles. A Cardinal holds a Cardinalate, votes for the next Pope in the conclave, and can take orders from the Head of Faith.
Cardinals exist in all three start dates.
The College holds up to 70 Cardinals.
Cardinalate titles are destroyed on succession. A Cardinal who becomes Pope or Antipope gives up their seat.
Cardinals of a Lay Clergy Rite cannot be elected Pope.
Added Papabile Score, which measures a Cardinal's standing in the next conclave.
Added Increase Papabile Score: spend Piety or gold to raise a Cardinal's Papabile Score.
Added Influence College of Cardinals Vote: pressure a Cardinal to cast their vote for your chosen candidate.
Added the Renounce the Papacy decision. A clerical ruler who renounces the Papacy is removed from every conclave shortlist. A Cardinal keeps their own vote. The renunciation can be reversed later.
Added a Cardinal Budget to the church treasury.
Added the Endow Masses decision. It spends treasury for Piety, and your subordinate clergy gain Piety and opinion of you.
Appoint Cardinal: as Head of Faith, raise a cleric to Cardinal.
Strip Cardinalate: dissolve a Cardinalate. Its holder stops being a Cardinal and loses their voice in the College.
Give Cardinal Order: as a Cardinal's superior, have them marshal church resources to carry out your will. Costs 50 Piety.
Request Cardinalate for Court Chaplain: petition the Head of Faith to raise your Court Chaplain into the College.
A new Pope chooses a regnal name in a dedicated interface. Female Popes get the option too.
Added the College of Cardinals window, with candidate shortlists and scoring tooltips. Alt+G opens it.
An Antipope who becomes Pope gains the College of Cardinals.
Added Papal Bulls, solemn decrees of a Christian Head of Faith backed by the authority of the Church. The Enact a Bull decision costs Piety. The Bulls are:
Permit a Tenet: endorse a Tenet as Permitted across the Faith and announce it to every ruler of the Faith.
Forbid a Tenet: mark a Tenet as Prohibited across the Faith and announce it to every ruler of the Faith.
Declare a Rite Heretical: name a divergent Rite of your Faith a heresy.
Proclaim the Age of Crusades: adopt Armed Pilgrimages as a Core Tenet of the Mainline Rite, opening the way to Great Holy Wars.
Added Church Authority, four levels of law that measure a theocratic ruler's power over their clergy and vassals. Issuing Bulls requires enough Church Authority.
Added the Send Legatine Mission decision. Spend treasury to send a legate to a County, improving its Development growth and Control for 10 years.

Added the Bend the Knee decision. During the Investiture Controversy, pledge to support the Church's claim to clerical appointments, and stand with the faithful when the Investiture Council is called.
Added the Ecumenical Council, an Activity where the clergy of Christendom and its most influential rulers gather to settle doctrine. It has a 25-year cooldown.

Guests split into Innovators and Conservatives. Debate phases run one month each. Events let guests sway the other side, duel over a point of doctrine, or bypass the cost with a matching Personal Tenet or trait.
A Council can change Core Tenets, rule on Doctrines, and set a Tenet's status.
Clergy, rulers with a clerical Puppet, and the host may vote.
Councils are a major source of Great Schism progress, for or against.
Rewards include Tenet and Doctrine changes, Fervor, Piety, opinion, and the Scholar lifestyle trait.
Added an Activity Planner widget for selecting Tenets and Doctrines.
Added the Investiture Council activity. It settles an Investiture Controversy on spiritual or temporal terms and decides who appoints the clergy.
Added Puppets: characters you control and can order to act on your behalf.
Realm Priest Puppet, made with Puppet Realm Priest: your Court Chaplain acts for you.
Clerical Ruler Puppet, made with Puppet Clerical Ruler: a member of the clergy outside your realm acts for you.
Secular Ruler Puppet, made with Puppet Secular Ruler: a ruler forced to do your bidding.
Excommunication
Holy Sites
Faith and Rite creation
Clerical Title requests
Cardinal appointments
Conversions
Monastic vows
Claims
Schemes
Imprisonment
War
Tributaries
Marriage and divorce

Great Projects
Puppets tab in the Intrigue window lets you manage your puppets.
Actions a Puppet can perform for you are marked with a Puppet banner on their buttons.
A Puppet pays the costs of their own actions and takes the blame for refusals.
Secular puppeteers have their own requirements for winning a Puppet over, separate from Spiritual Fulfillment.
Mandala God-Kings and the Son of Heaven can manipulate Rites without a Puppet.
The Realm Priest Puppet is disabled for characters with a Ministry or Kurultai.
Added decisions and interactions for founding and running Monastic Orders:
Found Monastic Order: build a temple holding in an empty barony of a chosen County. When it is finished, it becomes the seat of a new order focused on a Core Tenet of your choice.
Patronize Monastic Movement: found a new Monastic Order at once and transfer another order's leases within your domain to it.
Reform Monastic Endowment: spend gold for Piety, Spiritual Fulfillment, and the opinion of the orders' leaders.
Reform Order: as patron, bind an order you patronize to one of your Personal Tenets and to your own Rite.
Dissolve Order: destroy a Monastic Order.
Added a monastic funeral event chain for funerals held where a Monastic Order holds a lease.
Added Canonization. A Head of Faith can raise a departed member of their dynasty to sainthood and choose where to lay them to rest.

Added the Promulgate Word of Pious Deeds decision. Taken during a character's life, it spends Piety to either raise your election score for your superior's title or improve your chance of later canonization.
Added the Consecrate the Saint decision: pick the Cathedral or Holy Site in your realm where a saint is consecrated and laid to rest, so that they draw the faithful.
Added a Select a Patron Saint decision.
Added Proclaim the Living Word: become a Herald of your Faith.
Added saint titles for non-Christian Faiths, with Venerated Ancestor as a fallback. Examples:
Wali
Divus
Siddha
Kami
Added the Herald trait for living holy persons, with per-religion names. Examples:
Tzadik
Arhat
Sant
Zhenren
Sage
Ashavan
Added the Extract a Relic decision: take a relic from a saint buried in lands you control. The relic can then be enshrined in a Holy Site.

Added Sanctify Artifact: as Head of Faith, bless one of a character's artifacts, making it a holy relic of your Faith. Ask to Sanctify Artifact petitions a cleric to do the same for one of yours. Added a suggestion for it and a buried saint point of interest.

Every Rite can sanctify a baseline of devotional artifacts, so Sanctify Artifact works for Rites with few tenets. Vows of Poverty Rites cannot sanctify illustrious relics. They can sanctify humble artifacts of any quality.

Added Holy Myron, a consecrated oil made with the Prepare the Holy Myron decision. It sends your Court Chaplain to gather rare balsams and consecrate an Ampulla of Holy Myron, an artifact whose charges are spent on anointments.
Gift the Holy Myron: fill a fresh ampulla for another character, spending one charge for Piety and their gratitude.
Anoint an Artifact with Holy Myron: spend one charge to sanctify one of your artifacts, regardless of what your tenets would normally allow.
Added the Secure Pilgrim Routes decision, which adopts Armed Pilgrimages as a Core Tenet.
Added pilgrim badges as a new artifact type with their own badge slot.

notes.title: The Grand Cathedral and the Ecclesiastical Estate​

items.text: Added the Grand Cathedral, a Great Project built in three tiers: Romanesque, Gothic, and Flamboyant. Several characters can fund it, and each investor is rewarded on completion. If the founder dies, the reward reaches their heir.
The site must be its Archdiocese's capital and must not already hold a cathedral.

An event chain runs alongside construction: laying out the site, casting the bells, commissioning frescoes, contributing stained glass, building a cantoria, and preaching the first sermon once the west wall is up.
Added the Ecclesiastical Estate, the domicile of Clerical Title holders, with its own Cathedral Complex.
The character window uses church backgrounds that change as the domicile develops.
Added the Mass Conversion Great Project, which converts large swaths of Counties of unreformed Faiths.
Added the Proclaim the Kingdom of Heaven decision, which makes you holder of a new Hegemony-tier title, the Kingdom of Heaven.
Added the Establish a Dynasty decision, which lets a theocratic ruler start their own dynasty.
The Great Schism is now a tracked, playable event.

Great Schism progress comes from Ecumenical Councils, rulers crossing between the Rites, excommunications across the Rites, and County conversions in Holy Site Counties. Every source counts as a single grievance. Progress never decreases.
Players in the Christian Church Situation are notified whenever Great Schism progress accrues, and the participant groups show which side of the Schism each character is on.
Added three decisions, all requiring the Saeculum Obscurum Chapter and the progress threshold:
Cause the Great Schism
Prevent the Great Schism
Mend the Great Schism Through Diplomacy
Added the Sway Schism Stance interaction: urge a ruler to adopt your stance on the coming division of the Church.
Mending the Schism gives the mender's dynasty 10,000 Renown and a permanent modifier.
A Crisis Chapter ending only causes the Great Schism if the progress threshold has been met.
Added the Unite the Miaphysite Churches major decision.
Added the Religious Study scheme, which lets a character study a Rite in depth. The decision that starts it is named after your Faith's holy text, for example Study the Bible..
Added the Scholar lifestyle trait and the Renowned Exegete and Doctrinal Clarity outcomes.
Added an important action for excommunicated rulers. It explains how to lift the excommunication.
An Antipope you declare also becomes your Clerical Ruler Puppet.
Petition Antipope for Gold: request gold from your Antipope.
Seek Antipope's Indulgence: pay your Antipope gold for forgiveness and Piety, bypassing the Mainline Head of Faith.
Added a Pastoral Letter event and a Debate of East and West random event.
Added ritual celebration events, secular faith events and memories such as healing the sick with a king's touch, and a discovery event set.

notes.title: Added decisions tied to specific Personal Tenets

items.text: Invite Syncretic Exiles, for the syncretism tenets: invite exiles from a religion your personal syncretism recognizes. They settle in your Counties, raising Development and changing the local Faith or Rite. Costs a large amount of Piety.
Curse an Enemy, for the Adorcism tenet: perform a ritual against a rival or an opponent in one of your wars.
Seek Aid for War, for the Adorcism tenet: petition the spirits for aid in your current wars.
Take Confession: confess your sins to your Court Chaplain, losing Stress and gaining Spiritual Fulfillment.
Stage an Act of Devotion: hold a great public mass, exchanging Piety for Prestige. Once per decade, and only while your Fame is below Illustrious.
Sacrifice Wealth: spend gold to raise a County's Development growth and gain Spiritual Fulfillment.
Raise a Khachkar: commission an ancestral cross-stone in one of your Counties.
Receive Last Rites: prepare your soul as death nears, gaining Spiritual Fulfillment. It opens automatically when a character is close to death, and names a plausible killer.
Added the 867 bookmark Fathers of the Faithful.
Added the Slavic Rite story cycle in 867 for Rostislav. It follows the Moravian Mission and the birth of the Slavic Rite.
Added the Servants of God dynasty legacy for Christian dynasties, with five perks:
Private Devotions
Alms and Endowments: Head of Faith petitions are looked on more favorably, and the church treasury is more willing to fund your dynasty members' requests.
A Faithful Flock: dynasty members gain 50% more Tenet Popularity when evangelizing their Personal Tenets.
Mitre and Crosier: stronger candidate scores for Christian clerical appointments, a higher chance of being made a Cardinal, and more tax from ecclesiastical vassals.

Princes of the Church: dynasty members are stronger candidates for the Papal Throne, and can take the Guide the Christian Church decision regardless of rank or clerical office, with double the effect.
Guido's Guiding Light: Starting as Archbishop Guido of Milan, become Antipope and make the Ambrosian Rite the Mainline Rite.
The Two Swords: Have both the Holy Roman Emperor and the Pope as your Puppets at the same time.
Father's Best Side: Enshrine a relic taken from a saint of your own family in a Holy Site your Dynasty founded.
The Father, the Son, and the Holy Grandson: As a Theocrat, establish a Dynasty and hold an Archbishopric for three generations.
Servus Servorum Dei: Starting as a secular ruler of Duke tier or lower, or as a Count-tier cleric, become the Pope.
Papal Bull: Make your Puppet Pope sleep with your spouse.
Where There's a Will: Demand Church Succession from another ruler, then murder them and inherit their lands.
Home See Advantage: As an Archbishop, change a Tenet or Doctrine at an Ecumenical Council hosted in your own Cathedral.
Cardinal Sin: Starting as a non-Clergy ruler, have five members of your dynasty as Cardinals at the same time.
Holier Than Thou: Have three Personal Tenets and 100 Spiritual Fulfillment at the same time.

Added Rites. A Rite is a distinct tradition within a Faith, with its own Head of Rite, liturgy, Tenets, and map color. The Faith as a whole follows its Mainline Rite.
Every existing faith branch and school is now a Rite, including:

Added Divergence. A Rite that drifts far enough from its Faith's Mainline Rite counts as heresy. A Rite that reaches maximum Divergence immediately branches off as a new Faith.
Added the Head of Rite, who sits under the Head of Faith.
Added the Rite Creation window and the Create a Rite flow, which lets a character found a new Rite of their Faith.

Added Sway to Rite, which urges a character to adopt your Rite. It comes in three versions, for courtiers, vassals, and rulers, each with its own recipient list. Range is limited to the acting cleric's own realm and diocese.
Founding a Rite converts the founder's whole same-faith domain and court to the new Rite. Rulers who accept the founding conversion offer convert their domain and court too.
A Rite founded by a culture head takes its name from the religion, for example Polish Christianity.
Proselytizing to locals converts them to the traveler's own Rite.

Faith Fervor reacts to the distribution of Rites. Fervor decreases when new Rites are created, and declines faster as Rites grow Divergent from the Mainline. Fervor increases when Rites are reined in, or declared heretical and split from the Faith.
Faiths found new Rites as they grow. New Rites have a grace period against instant reconversion.
Gender preference laws, crimes, and liturgical language are set per Rite.
Rites can override special Faith and Religion localizations such as the name of the High God.
State Faith is now State Rite.
Heresies now break out in Faiths whose Fervor has fallen below 40. Outbreak chance rises as Fervor falls further.

notes.title: Added interactions for dealing with the orders

items.text: Take Vows: ask someone to take the vows and join the clergy.
Ask to Take Monastic Vows: ask someone to join a Monastic Order.
Demand Child for the Cloister: demand a child, descendant, or underage courtier in someone's care as a Devoted courtier of your own, removing them from succession.
Bestow a Monastery: lease a temple holding to a Monastic Order, gaining Piety, Spiritual Fulfillment, and better access to the order.
Revoke Lease: take a leased holding back from an order.
Monastic Orders weigh the donor's Rite when accepting donations and leases, with a large penalty when the donor's Rite prohibits the tenet the order was founded on.

Added the Form Knightly Sellsword Band decision. It turns an accolade knight into a mercenary company that stays allied to you, sends yearly gifts of gold, and recruits a Men-at-Arms regiment based on the accolade or the knight's culture.
Added a Holy Orders map mode. It shows leased holdings linked to their orders, and government icons for each order.
Added Eminent Holy Sites, a rank above regular Holy Sites.
Faiths can have a limited amount of Eminent Holy Sites (usually three); only Eminent Holy Sites affect all characters of a Faith
Faiths can now have more total Holy Sites than before - up to nine in total
Some Holy Sites were shuffled / added throughout the world, including but not limited to:
Lhasa replaces Muara Takus as an eminent Vajrayana Holy Site, which brings the Jowo Shakyamuni into play.
Antioch replaces Aksum as Miaphysitism's third eminent Holy Site. Aksum remains a regular Holy Site.
Mahayana has three extra regular Holy Sites in China/Japan: Mount Wutai, Luoyang and Nara
Vajrayana has two extra regular Holy Sites in Dali and Pagan
Added the Holy Site window and the Create Holy Site window, with four Holy Site actions:
Elevate Holy Site: raise a Holy Site to Eminent. If the Faith is at its Eminent maximum, demote one first.
Demote Holy Site: return an Eminent Holy Site to a normal one.
Abandon Holy Site: remove a Holy Site from your Faith. Its enshrined relics go to the County holder.
Adopt Holy Site: add an existing Holy Site inside your realm to your Faith. Limited to Holy Sites within your Religion unless you have the Adoptionism tenet
You can Create new Holy Sites where none existed before
Ten new types of Dynamic Holy Site types have been added
Faiths cannot duplicate multiple Dynamic Holy Site types
Creating new Holy Sites requires having Holy Relics of sufficient quality

Elevating a new regular Holy Site to an Eminent Holy Site can be done via a separate step. If the Faith is at the maximum for Eminent Holy Sites, you might first need to Demote an existing Eminent Holy Site first.
Holy Sites allow Enshrining of up to three Holy Relic Artifacts
There are both local and global modifiers on Holy Sites that scale depending on the total amount of Artifact quality levels Enshrined in a Holy Site
Holy Sites without any Enshrined Holy Relics (for the correct Faith) are considered inactive for the purposes of providing holy site benefits, even the unscaled benefits

An Enshrined Artifact is no longer owned by a Character, but by the Holy Site. Removing and adding Holy Relics can be done by Rulers that hold the Holy Site, by Heads of Faith, or by religious rulers who control the Clerical Region (Archdiocese) it is in.
Enshrining or removing Enshrined Holy Relics will give/lose Piety, and will make character like/dislike you more
The creation of a new Faith grants three free Holy Site actions (create, demote, elevate, abandon, adopt)
Holy Sites without a special building but with Enshrined Holy Relics are now considered minor Religious Points of Interest
Holy Relics are now more dynamic
You can create new Holy Relics by sanctifying
Added Antipopes and the Challenger Head of Faith, a rival head of your Rite.
Declare an Antipope: install a cleric of your Rite as a rival Head of Faith. The candidate adopts your Rite and becomes an independent ruler.
Proclaim Yourself Antipope: declare yourself the Challenger Head of Faith. For Muslims the decision is Challenge the Caliph.
Added the Challenge Head of Faith casus belli. If the challenger wins, they become Head of Faith and their Rite becomes the Mainline Rite. Co-religionists may join either side.
Added the Depose Antipope casus belli, which removes a rival's Antipope.
Added the Humiliation casus belli against Theocracies. It takes gold from their treasury and lowers their authority. Secular rulers can use it, and the AI only uses it when impious and greedy.
Added Branched Rite Frequency. By default a Faith waits 3 to 18 years between new Rites. Settings run from Much More Often (1 to 8 years) to Much Less Often (8 to 45 years), or None.

Added Branched Rite Amount. By default a Faith supports one extra Rite per 70 Counties and founds its first at 140. Settings run from Many More (one per 35, first at 70) to Far Fewer (one per 140, first at 280).
Added Heresy Outbreak Frequency, from a quarter as likely to four times as likely.
The Randomized Faiths game rule is now Randomized Faiths & Rites. It assigns each ruler a random Faith and a random Rite within it, drawn from all Faiths in the game.
Added Expand Nomadic Region: Northeastern Asia. The Nomadic setting puts the region on the Great Steppe nomadic mechanics. Requires Khans of the Steppe.
Added a portrait light rotation offset so a character's lighting stays consistent between the event window and Barbershop camera angles.

Added icons for succession types, shown next to the Primary Heir label.
Map modes with sub map modes now show them as round buttons above the map mode name. The lobby map has a sub map mode switcher too.
Added hotkeys for the Rite and Culture buttons on the HUD: Alt+T and Alt+R. The Rite button now sits above Culture, as in the character window.
Reduced the size of sheep and horses on the map.
Dithered the scene output to remove gradient banding, most visible in ground fog.
Added the Study Faith scheme. It lets rulers learn the Tenets and Doctrines of nearby Faiths and Rites, and possibly convert once they have learned enough. A Faith you fully know cannot be studied.

Added a Doctrine that tracks how a Faith persists its traditions: orally, through myths, or with a written code. It decides whether rulers can learn a Faith by letter or need a tutor present in person.

Added the Find Adherent of Faith scheme. It lets rulers summon adherents of Faiths in their realm to study their Faith. In special circumstances rulers can also look for hidden adherents of dead Faiths, though the search can be long and arduous.
Added Hegemony support for Rites, Faiths, and Cultures, and lists for hegemonies of a given Culture, Rite, or Faith.
